justify_why_gaps_are_missing.justification: The x-axis (Lag, hours) shows a continuous range around the circadian period (≈24–48 h) with regularly spaced tick marks and no sudden numeric jumps that would require an axis break.
The y-axis (Rhythmicity index) displays a continuous numeric range (≈0–0.9) with regular tick spacing; no omitted interval or discontinuity is evident.
The x-axis (Circadian component) runs continuously from 0 to 1 with even tick spacing — no omitted ranges or jumps requiring a break.

The y-axis is labeled log10(Noise component) and is presented on a logarithmic scale (consistent tick spacing for log scale). A log scale is appropriate for the large dynamic range and no axis-break symbol is necessary.

Top subpanel x-axis (Period, hours) is continuous over ~21–33 h with regular tick spacing; bottom subpanel x-axis is explicitly labeled as log(amplitude), indicating a log-transformed axis appropriate for the wide range — no axis break required.
Density axes are continuous probability/density scales without omitted intervals; no discontinuities observed that would need marking.
The x-axis is categorical (cell lines) and shows each category explicitly; axis breaks are not applicable or needed for categorical axes.
The y-axis (Ridge length, hours) shows a continuous numeric range with regular tick intervals (e.g., 24, 48, 72, …); there are no omitted ranges requiring a break.
Polar/angular axes are shown continuously (phase in radians) with regular angular ticks; axis breaks are not applicable to circular polar plots.
Radial (probability/normalized count) scales are continuous and displayed appropriately for polar histograms; no omitted intervals or breaks are present.
Panel F is a polar histogram of phase differences; angular axis is continuous and appropriately labeled — no axis break needed.
Radial normalization/probability scale is continuous and no discontinuity or omitted interval is apparent.
Time axis spans ~0–100 hours with regular tick spacing; no sections are omitted or compressed that would require a break marker.
Signal (arb. units) axis is continuous with symmetric range about zero; no abrupt numeric jumps or omitted ranges are visible.
The x-axis (amplitude exponential decay rate, γ) shows a continuous numeric range with appropriately spaced tick marks; no omitted interval or jump is evident.

The y-axis (Amplitude, A0) spans orders of magnitude but is presented using a scale appropriate for the range (tick spacing indicates orders of magnitude). No truncated or skipped region is apparent that would require a visual axis break.
